PullRequest.Title: Build the pending list's clock touch events without the Touch constructor in desktop WebKit
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes `REG-WEBKIT-TOUCH-CONSTRUCTOR`, which fails main CI [498256](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=498256) on macOS ARM64 WebKit browser unit tests and will fail the official's macOS unit job the same way.

## What fails

#348704 added `Sessions - pending list items › clock touches bypass list gestures without suppressing the preview click`. It builds its events with `new mainWindow.Touch(...)`. Desktop WebKit doesn't allow constructing `Touch` and throws `TypeError: Illegal constructor`, so the test fails before it dispatches anything. It's deterministic, 1 of 56,423 in 498256.

## What this changes (test-only)

A small `createTouchEvent` helper in the test:

- Where `Touch` can be constructed (Chromium, Firefox), it builds the same real `Touch` and `TouchEvent` as before.
- Where it can't (desktop WebKit), it dispatches a plain `Event` of the same type that carries `touches`, `targetTouches` and `changedTouches` lists with the members `Gesture` reads (`length`, `item()`, `identifier`, `target`, `pageX`, `pageY`).

So WebKit keeps the coverage and isn't skipped. Product code doesn't change.

## Validation

- The test file passes in WebKit, Chromium and Firefox (27 tests).
- With the fallback forced in WebKit and Chromium, the test passes.
- **Red check:** with the product's `Gesture.ignoreTarget(indicator)` removed, the test fails on both the native and the fallback path (`endPrevented: true`). The fallback still catches the regression the test was written for.
- `tsc -p src/tsconfig.json --noEmit` reports no errors in the touched file.

> Authored with Copilot

Scenarios.CriticalPath: Create a one-session list, read the indicator bounds, construct two events, synchronously dispatch touchstart and touchend, click the indicator, then await the existing zero-delay timeout before assertions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read DOM geometry and synchronously dispatch browser events through the existing gesture listeners.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One geometry read, two touch-event dispatches and one click per test invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same geometry read and event dispatch sequence already occurred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous test-main-thread work before the assertions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize the scheduled-card cache key and render/show its DOM hover.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One key calculation for one scheduled request and one initial card construction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same click created the same card and key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously on the existing preview click before the test asserts its text.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Exactly two helper calls and one touch point in one test; one scheduled request with short text, no attachments and no actions. This helper is not used by production code or other tests.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The two event constructions and dispatches execute serially on the browser main thread. No worker, subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database or network operation is added or reached by the changed event construction.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No helper cache or retry loop. Native construction now creates two Touch objects instead of sharing one; the additional allocation is bounded. The existing per-template scheduled-card cache and disposal ownership are unchanged; this test opens one initially cold card.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the complete diff and helper call sites establish exactly two calls; gesture cleanup deletes the active touch on touchend, and test-owned list/hover resources retain their existing disposal.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No timings were measured; the extra native Touch object is constant-size work in one test, not a realistic scaling regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression: only bounded test-local construction changes, with unchanged event processing, preview rendering and cleanup.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run the same clock-touch preview test on desktop WebKit where Touch construction throws.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each of the two helper calls catches the unsupported constructor and builds a plain Event with three small touch-list arrays. The existing gesture handlers then process the events and the preview click renders one card before assertions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Construct and dispatch in-memory browser events, read indicator geometry and show the DOM preview.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two failed native constructor attempts, two fallback events, one geometry read and one preview click.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: WebKit threw on the first Touch constructor after the existing geometry read, so this test never reached dispatch or preview creation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Bounded synchronous work on this test's main thread.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Compute the existing scheduled-card key and construct the preview for the fixture's single request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One key calculation and one card construction for one short request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This existing product path was not reached by this test on WebKit because event construction failed; successful browsers already exercised it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Completes during the preview click before assertions.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Two constructor attempts, two fallback events, six touch-list wrappers and one touch point per test invocation; no input-dependent loop or repeated scheduling is introduced.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serial event construction and synchronous dispatch; one existing zero-delay timeout. No changed or transitively reached subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database or network call for these plain-text fixtures.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Unsupported Touch construction is attempted twice without caching, a fixed cardinality. The fallback's arrays and item closures are owned by the two local events, not a persistent collection. Existing preview caching and test teardown are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the only two helper call sites, one-point fixture, gesture touch deletion and preview disposal are explicit in the inspected code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Static review only; exception and DOM operation durations were not measured. The test now intentionally completes previously unreachable coverage, with fixed small allocations.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added work restores a previously failing test and is bounded; it introduces no product hot-path work or unbounded retention. This is a compatibility correction, not a concrete performance-regression fix.
